Q: Automate Downloading Reports then Copy/Pasting Them to Google Sheets A:

Google Sheets has an API: https://developers.google.com/workspace/sheets/api/guides/concepts. Simulating user actions using Selenium seems like way more work than is necessary. I don't know what the capabilities of your "system" are, but I'd just set up an API on your end to download the documents, then reach out to the Sheets API and instruct it to plug the data in wherever you want.

Q: Can I disable Driver Signature Enforcement on Windows 7 and 10 programatically A:

I've had some success with DSE Patcher It's in the bin folder, just click it, and click disable, you should be able to install your driver now. WindowsD seems to do the job too, just install it, run wind64 /w, restart your system and it should work. Edit: As of this writing, it does not work for the 24H2 version of win11. As usual, Microsoft changed stuff around, when I find a workaround I will try to add it here. Update: EfiGuard disables it on 24H2. BootBypass working on 26H1

Programatically, look at this blog to disable it permananently, perhaps a talented dev can automate the process.

Q: Pygame only displays a grey window A:

You need a game loop that continually does the following:

  • calls pygame.display.flip() -- this will update the screen with new changes
  • calls pygame.event.get() -- this is the most important because otherwise, the event queue will not get flushed and the OS will assume your program is being unresponsive. You can't have things like sleep(5) in PyGame.

Q: "Defend" Against Multiple ANSI Styles A:

One idea would be to create a function that filters out the unwanted styles.

library(cli)

sty_1 <- combine_ansi_styles(
  style_italic,
  style_bold,
  style_strikethrough
)

filter_combined_style <- function(x, combined_style, exclude = c()) {
  env <- environment(combined_style)
  all_styles <- env$styles
  
  filtered_styles <- all_styles[!names(all_styles) %in% exclude]
  
  for (style in filtered_styles) {
    x <- paste0(style$open, x, style$close)
  }
  
  structure(x, class = "cli_ansi_string")
}

Then any style that we want to defend against will be added to exclude.

"Example text" |> filter_combined_style(sty_1, 
                                        exclude = c("italic", "strikethrough"))

<cli_ansi_string>

[1]Example text

"Example text" |> filter_combined_style(sty_1, 
                                        exclude = c("italic"))

<cli_ansi_string>

[1]Example text

"Example text" |> filter_combined_style(sty_1)

<cli_ansi_string>

[1]Example text

Q: Delete a section of a file Bash Script A:

Regular expression; The point here is that matching on line numbers, and fixed strings, does not generalize. There is a principle in software engineering that apples here; 'DRY' (a.k.a. Don't Repeat Yourself) to the sed command; esentially your lead system admin want's you to figure out how to use one command to do many (e.g., 3) things.

As for a advice: Read up on what does '^$' mean in regular expression (The answer is in the manpage for re_format man re_format) and then consider what differs between ^# and ^[^#]. That will get your head around what's going on.

As for your question:

how would you grep the first comment, last comment, and then anything in between those comments delete

Also, I apologise to your lead system admin for just answering:

Try a single awk instead of multiple grep and sed stuff (albeit there is a nasty way to use a single sed, I'd advise against it):

e.g.:

START='# begin-block'
END='# end-block'
awk -v S="$START" -v E="$END" '
  $0 == S { in=1; next }
  $0 == E && in { in=0; next }
  !in
' file

And, my final advice is to understand why this awk strategy is DRY, and helpful to your scenario. (as a beginner, you can have an LLM explain this to you)

Other useful concepts that may have been overlooked (e.g., for a beginner):

  • delimiters (e.g., why patterns instead of lines)
  • file parsing (e.g., why reach for awk)
  • regular expression (namely what Extended RE can do rather than just how)
  • coupling - Namely: bash pipes and pipeline type design (in the context of system's engineering)
  • The key differences between the tools: awk, ast-grep, grep, and sed

Q: How to find Optimal Opcache Memory Size? A:

Recommended php.ini settings ¶

The following settings are generally recommended as providing good performance:

opcache.memory_consumption=128
opcache.interned_strings_buffer=8
opcache.max_accelerated_files=4000
opcache.revalidate_freq=60
opcache.fast_shutdown=1 ; prior to PHP 7.2.0
opcache.enable_cli=1
